route: regular Old French feminisation of -our/-eur nouns
notes: NOT a direct Latin inheritance, and NOT an exception: Old French regularly feminised this class (cf. douleur, peur). Littré: "était féminin dans l'ancienne langue, comme tous les noms ainsi dérivés"; Grevisse: "n'avait, dans l'ancienne langue, que le genre féminin". The singular was masculinised only in the 16th-17th c. by grammarians aligning usage with the Latin etymon. In the Middle French of the Mirouer, feminine amour is the period norm.

route: Romance formation; masculine regardless of etymon
notes: le néant. Substantivised indefinite pronoun, masculine by the default the French system assigns to that class. The *ne gentem derivation is a hypothesis (Körting 1896, recorded by TLFi, accepted by FEW), not established; TLFi marks it "prob.". Note the etymon head gens, gentis is feminine, so the masculine is in no case inherited. Configuration in the text: a grammatically feminine Soul annihilated INTO a grammatically masculine void.
Agrees with the noun it modifies (l'ame anientie is feminine because ame is); has no gender of its own.
